page.layout: One page of text in a single column; a woodcut initial opens the Concio paragraph; a centred heading with a verse reference; no marginal notes; signature at the foot.

main_text.l: tale proferre. In vobis ergo omnis culpa hæ-
ret, nec repudiatis vxoribus, sed turpissim-
æ adulteræ similes estis, quæ marito relicto a-
matores suos sectatur, &c. Quoad ergo con-
silium siue priuilegium per Mosem datum,
ista repudiorum ratio mala non erat: merito
autem reprehendi debebant Iudæi, qui hanc
in effrenem suæ libidinis licentiam conuer-
terant: quæ causa est, quod illos Dominus
nunc arctioribus terminis constringit.
Habemus in his exemplum memorabile,
quæ optima sit in legibus ciuilibus dispen-
sandi ratio, & quando illa admitti, quando i-
tem legum authoritas seuerius vrgeri ac re-
tineri debeat. Christus Iesus Dominus &
seruator noster det nobis intellectum in
omnibus, Amen.
CONCIO XLVI
Matth. 19. -
DICVNT ei discipuli eius: Si
ad ipsum modum habet causa
hominis cum uxore[?], non ex-
pedit contrahere matrimoni-
um. Qui dixit illis: Non omnes capa-
ces sunt huius dicti, sed quibus datum
est. Sunt enim eunuchi, qui de matris
utero sic nati sunt: & sunt eunuchi, qui
facti sunt eunuchi ab hominibus: & sunt

page.notes: The woodcut initial is a decorated D set in a framed box; the first word is DICVNT with the initial D from the woodcut. The line "uxore" is followed by a curved mark that I could not identify with certainty, so I read it as a stop-like sign with [?]. The page number "195" is a long, italic-style numeral; the final digit is doubtful. The running head "NVPTIALES." has a decorated initial N and the V in place of U is kept as printed. The signature "T 4" stands at the foot. The text breaks off mid-sentence at the end of the page ("& sunt"), which continues on the next page.
